Construction of spirooxindole-fused
spiropyrazolones containing contiguous three
stereogenic centres via [3 + 2] annulation utilizing
a ferrocene derived bifunctional phosphine
catalyst†
Wenjun Luo, Bingxuan Shao, Jingyi Li, Xiao Xiao, Dingguo Song, Fei Ling
 and
Weihui Zhong
 *
A ferrocene-derived bifunctional phosphine-catalyzed enantioselective [3 + 2] annulation of γ-substituted
allenoates with pyrazoloneyldiene oxindoles is investigated for the construction of spiro-cyclopentene-
linked oxindole and pyrazolone compounds, which bear three consecutive stereocenters and two vicinal
spiroquaternary chiral centers, in good chemical yields (up to 95%) with excellent regio-, diastereo- (dr >
19 : 1) and enantioselectivities (up to 98% ee).
Spirocyclic compounds, bearing at least one quaternary
carbon, are valuable structural mofits due to their broad appli-
cations as biomedicinal natural molecules and pharmaceuti-
cals.1 Among multifarious spirocyclic compounds, spiro-cyclo-
pentane-oxindole (SCPO) 2 and spiro-cyclopentane-pyrazolone
(SCPP)3 have attracted extensive interest from pharmaceutical
and organo-synthetic communities due to their myriad bio-
logical activities (Fig. 1). For example, SCPOs I and II have
been reported as natural compounds,
4 and III is an inhibitor
of p53/MDM2. 5 Moreover, SCPPs IV and V have been recog-
nized as inhibitors of type-4 phosphodiesterase, 6 and VI serves
as a PPAR antagonist. 7
The combination of pharmacophores is an e ﬀective strategy
for discovering new bioactive compounds in pharmaceutical
research.8 Therefore, we are interested in exploring organocata-
lytic methods to construct spiro-cyclopentene sca ﬀolds linking
oxindoles to pyrazolones, which can be potential and trendy
tactics for drug discovery. Additionally, it has been envisioned
that the phosphine-mediated [3 + 2] annulation reaction
between allene as a C
3 synthon and an appropriate C 2
synthon, activated pyrazoloneyldiene oxindole, is applicable to
construct spiro-oxindole cyclopentene-pyrazolone (Scheme 1),
since the first phosphine-catalyzed [3 + 2] cycloadditions of
allenoates with electron-deficient olens to generate functiona-
lized cyclopentene rings were reported by Lu in 1995. 9
Mono-, di-, or tri-substituted activated alkenes are routinely
utilized as reaction partners with allenes for the synthesis of
cyclopentenes,
10 but the utilization of tetra-substituted alkenes
was extremely limited. To the best of our knowledge, there was
only one limited literature study by Lu, who reported the [3 +
2] annulation of allenes and tetra-substituted alkenes to
produce dispirocyclic oxindole structural motifs.
11 Very
recently, structurally novel bispiro-pyrazolone-3,3 ′-oxindoles
were synthesized via [3 + 2] annulation of Morita –Baylis–
Hillman carbonates with pyrazoloneyldiene oxindoles in excel-
lent yields, with diastereospecificity and high enantio-
selectivity catalyzed by ( S)-SITCP.

excellent study and our continuing interest in ferrocenyl-phos-
phine catalysis, 12 we speculated that the spiro-cyclopentene
linking oxindole and pyrazolone could be obtained by the
[3 + 2] annulation of tetra-substituted activated alkenes derived
from oxindole and pyrazolone with γ-substituted allenoates.
To test the feasibility, the [3 + 2] annulation reaction was
examined with ethyl 4-phenylbuta-2,3-dienoate 1a and pyrazo-
loneyldiene oxindole 2a in the presence of various phosphine
catalysts. According to our previous works,
13 when potassium
carbonate was chosen as the additive, the desired [3 + 2]
product 3aa was formed in 90% yield, with high diastereo-
selectivity (dr > 19 : 1) and regioselectivity (only the γ-adduct)
under the catalysis of triphenylphosphine in toluene at room
temperature (Table 1, entry 1). Then our previously designed
bifunctional chiral ferrocenylphosphines ( P1 and P2) were sub-
jected to the [3 + 2] annulation reaction and the desired
product 3aa was obtained with moderate ee values (65% and
68%) and good yields (Table 1, entries 2 and 3), respectively.
Next, to verify the e ﬃciency of phosphine catalysts, various
ferrocene derived bifunctional phosphine catalysts were inves-
tigated (Table 1, entries 4 –9). Catalyst P4 performed well and
led to the desired product 3aa with 75% yield and 81% ee
(Table 1, entry 4), which indicated that the 3,5-bis(trifluoro-
methyl) group on the benzene ring was beneficial for enantio-
selectivity. Based on the above-mentioned analysis, a further
trial of phosphine-ferrocene chiral catalysts was conducted.
These results demonstrated that catalyst P8, reported by
Zhang’s group,
14 exhibited more superior reactivity and stereo-
controllability, a ﬀording the product 3aa with 85% yield and
87% ee (Table 1, entries 7 –9). Gratifyingly, the enantio-
selectivity was improved to 98% ee, when decreasing the reac-
tion temperature from room temperature to −20 °C (Table 1,
entries 10 –12). Solvent screenings showed that other solvents
failed to give better results than toluene (Table 1, entries
13–15). Thus, the optimal reaction conditions are 10 mol% of
P8 as the catalyst, 10 mol% of potassium carbonate as the
additive and toluene as the solvent at −20 °C (Scheme 3).
With the optimal conditions in hand, the substrate scope
of both γ-substituted allenoates 1 and pyrazoloneyldiene oxi-
ndole components 2 was evaluated. Variation of the R
1
group showed that benzene rings with electron-withdrawing
or electron-donating groups at the 5-position (Scheme 2,
3aa–3ae) and the 7-position (Scheme 2, 3af–3am) gave the
desired products with good yields (79 –93%) and excellent
stereogenic control (90 –98% ee). Besides, when R 1 was 6-Cl
or H, the desired products were also obtained with high
yields and ee values (Scheme 2, 3aj and 3ak). Subsequently,
γ-substituted allenoates 1 with di ﬀerent ester groups on the
side chain were studied smoothly. However, the substrate
derived from benzyl acrylate a ﬀorded a lower ee value
than that from methyl acrylate or ethyl acrylate (Scheme 2,
3ak–3ck).

Further investigations of both N-substituent of the oxindole
moiety R 3 and N-substituent of the pyrazolone moiety R 4 were
performed with 4-phenyl-2,3-butadienoate 1a. However, the
substituted benzyl group (R 3) on oxindole led to lower stereose-
lectivities than the benzyl group, especially when R 3 was 4-iso-
propylbenzyl (70% ee) (Scheme 2, 3al–3ap). To our delight,
methyl (R 3) was well accommodated (Scheme 2, 3aq). Both the
electron-withdrawing and electron-donating groups (R 4) at the
1-position on aromatic pyrazolone could provide favourable ee
values (Scheme 2, 3ar and 3as). In addition, the absolute con-
figuration of 3ag was confirmed by X-ray crystallography
(CCDC 1961000†).15

Based on the previous reports, 16 a possible mechanism and
an activation model were proposed in Scheme 4. Initially, the
ferrocene-derived bifunctional phosphine attacked 1a creating
the zwitterionic intermediate Int-I, which subsequently under-
went γ-addition to the more electron-deficient carbon of pyra-
zoloneyldiene oxindole 2 to give intermediate II. Then, II was
converted into III through intramolecular Michael addition.
Finally, a proton transfer followed along with the release of the
chiral phosphine catalyst and yielded the [3 + 2] annulation
product spiro-cyclopentene compound 3 combined with oxi-
ndole and pyrazolone.
Conclusions
In conclusion, we have developed a highly regio-, diastereo-
and enantioselective methodology to construct spiro-cyclopen-
tene-linked oxindole and pyrazolone compounds, which bear
three consecutive stereocenters and two vicinal spiroquatern-
ary chiral centers (dr > 19 : 1 and ee up to 98%) via the enantio-
selective [3 + 2] annulation reaction of γ-substituted allenoates
with pyrazoloneyldiene oxindole by ferrocene-derived bifunc-
tional phosphine P8 as a catalyst. E ﬀorts to explore a more
eﬀective chiral ferrocenylphosphine catalyst and biological
evaluations of our synthetic spiro-oxindole cyclopentene-pyra-
zolones are underway in our laboratory.
